artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan carrying the batching-by-default doctrine to seven points of use, adding a narrowness qualifier and owner-blocked carve-out to Rule 1, and shipping update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add with a write-time cycle refusal that reuses validate-state.sh's existing Kahn check.

memory_candidates.content: When a planned edit targets an eagerly-loaded context file (anything feeding the assembled .claude/CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/*.md), check the eager-context budget BEFORE planning the addition: verify-deploy.sh Gate 20 sub-check B compares measure-eager-context.sh --check's 'TOTAL: <bytes> B' line against orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes and fail()s unconditionally on any regression above it. Headroom is routinely single-digit bytes (measured 9 B at one point), and baseline_bytes must never be silently re-derived, so an addition to an eager file is effectively required to be byte-neutral. The proven pattern, recorded four times in the baseline note's own history, is: relocate equivalent-or-greater duplicated detail from the eager file into a non-eager home, VERIFY the relocated text is present there before cutting the eager copy, then add. A plan that treats an eager-file addition as a free token cost will fail the final gate.
